proved_step: statement: Unique-witness selector lemma. Let R be a relation on inputs x and b-bit strings w, and suppose the prefix-extension predicate E(x,p) = 1 iff there exists w in {0,1}^b extending p with R(x,w) holds is decidable by a deterministic algorithm in time T. If for a given x there is exactly one w with R(x,w), that witness can be found using at most b calls to E and O(b) additional work. At prefix p, query E(x,p0); append 0 if the answer is 1, and otherwise append 1. Proof: initially the empty prefix has an extension by existence. Inductively, the maintained prefix p has an extension w*. If E(x,p0)=1, choosing p0 retains an extension. Otherwise no extension starts with 0, so w* starts with 1 and p1 retains it. After b steps the prefix has length b, so its only extension is itself and R(x,p) holds. Uniqueness identifies it as the unique witness. Thus uniqueness removes any need to choose among multiple completed witnesses, but does not provide an algorithm for E; a resource improvement still requires a bound for prefix extendibility.

statement: Lexicographic selector lemma. Let R(x,w) be any relation with witnesses w in {0,1}^b, and suppose at least one witness exists for a fixed x. Define E(x,p)=1 exactly when some R-witness extends prefix p. The lexicographically least R-witness can be found using at most b queries to E and O(b) additional bit operations. Start with the empty prefix p. At each position query E(x,p0); append 0 if it is 1, and append 1 otherwise. Proof: Inductively, p has at least one witness extension. If E(x,p0)=1, every witness extending p0 precedes every witness extending p1, so the least witness extending p also extends p0. If E(x,p0)=0, all witness extensions of p extend p1, so the least one does too. Thus after each query p remains a prefix of the lexicographically least witness. After b queries p has length b and equals that witness. Consequently, if E is decidable in time T per query, canonical witness search takes at most bT+O(b) time, excluding the cost of supplying x and any cost not included in E. This gives a precise search-to-extension reduction but alone gives no bound on E for canonical Search-MCSP witnesses.
